newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ross says gets Solomons mine lease.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ross says gets Solomons mine lease.

text.p: Ross Mining NL said on Wednesday that it had been granted a mining lease from the Solomon Islands government enabling it start construction of its Gold Ridge gold mine project.
The government has also executed a mining agreement setting out the terms and conditions for development of the mine, Ross said.
"At this stage, the mining lease has been signed," a spokesman for the prime minister of the Solomons, Solomon Mamaloni told Reuters by telephone from Honiara.
The spokesman said he was unable to comment on what if any impact a constitutional challenge lodged against Ross by some landowners in the mine area would have on the project.
The challenge was lodged on Monday.

Australian law firm Slater and Gordon, which represents Solomon Island villagers seeking to negotiate a new compensation package over the mine, said on Tuesday it would consider further legal actions against Ross if the project was granted the lease.

Despite official environmental approvals earlier this year from the Minister of Energy, Water and Mineral Resources, Slater and Gordon lawyer Nick Styant-Brown said the nearby Tetri River faced pollution caused by mine sediment.
This would have an impact on villagers who depend on the river system for their livelihood, Styant-Brown said recently.
Slater and Gordon lawyers were unavailable for comment.
Ross Mining has maintained its environmental system would enable it to contain sediment from the mine
John Lawton, a director of Ross, said the company would be assessing the implications of the legal action over the next few days.
However, planning and infrastructre were in place to start construction of the project, expected to cost A$61.6 million, Lawton said.
"The bottom line is that we've got the mining lease and they can't take that away from us," Lawton told Reuters.
The project's design calls for production of around one million ounces of gold over 10 years at an average cash cost of under A$300 an ounce.
The mine is scheduled to to pour its first gold in March 1998.

Slater and Gordon last year successfully won a compensation package for villagers in Papua New Guinea who had lodged environmental claims against The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd over the discharge of mine tailings from the Ok Tedi copper mine into the Fly River system.
